findings.severity: unsafe: unbounded aggregate allocation (V4-02), out of memory on a realistic document
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/export_set.rs:456-499 (views and renders BTreeMaps); LinearFrame.pixels is Vec<[f32; 4]> (render.rs:281)
findings.what: export.run keeps every view copy and every 1x linear render in `views` and `renders` until the run ends. Each render is 16 bytes per pixel, and up to 1 GiB at MAX_VIEW_PIXELS (64 Mi pixels). Only the per-render size and the file count (1024) are bounded. Nothing bounds the running total. `planned` is grouped by job (one job's settings are pushed together, :421-452), so a finished job's render is never read again.
findings.scenario: A brand document with 60 artboards of 2048 by 2048 (4 Mi pixels, 64 MiB per render), each marked PNG: export.run holds about 3.75 GiB of renders before it returns. With 4096 by 4096 boards it holds 15 GiB, and the process aborts on allocation failure instead of refusing typed.
findings.fix: Keep only the current job: before the `views.entry`, when p.job differs from the previous job, call views.clear() and renders.clear(). Optionally refuse `export_too_large` when the sum of 1x frame pixels in one job exceeds a budget. No test change is needed: the 8-file test still passes.

findings.certainty: READ (mechanism); the cropped pixels are UNVERIFIED (not rendered)
findings.severity: wrong answer: a stroked (or shadowed) layer target exports cropped
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/export_set.rs:292 (vector frame = Viewer::layer_bounds), vector/arrange.rs:226-240 (bounds_of = nib path_bounds, geometry only); export_set.rs:321-325 (the board becomes that frame); render.rs:440-442 (the render frames the first board)
findings.what: A layer target's frame is its path geometry bounds, with no stroke width and no effect extent. The view copy's first board is set to that frame and the render clips to it. A centred or outside stroke loses its outer part on every edge, and a drop shadow is lost. Each PNG, JPG, SVG viewBox and PDF page of the layer is cut at the path. With use_absolute_bounds false, STU-IO-112's default is the rendered extent, not the geometry. The lane's cut list says only 'use_absolute_bounds reads the same path bounds', which does not cover this. The tests use stroke_on: false (viewer_artboard_export.rs:24), so nothing catches it.
findings.scenario: Draw a 60 by 48 rectangle with stroke_on true and stroke_width 8, centre-aligned. export.set_settings on it with [{format: PNG, suffix: @2x, SCALE 2}] gives 120 by 96 instead of 136 by 112, and the outer 4 px of the stroke are cut on each side.
findings.fix: Inflate the vector frame by the layer's stroke extent: half the width for a centre stroke, the full width for an outside stroke, times the miter limit for miter joins, using the layer's appearance or design records, plus any effect offset and blur the renderer applies. Add one stroked-icon assert. If the lead defers this, at least declare it in the lane cut list and the module doc, and push a `frame_is_path_bounds` note into the file receipt when the layer has a stroke.

findings.certainty: READ (missing checks); UNVERIFIED (Windows device-name behaviour per Windows version)
findings.severity: low: a partial run that the module doc says cannot happen, and a possible silent drop
findings.what: (a) The plan checks the output size (ow*oh) and the horizontal pass (ow*h), but not the 1x render (w*h). render.rs:462 refuses canvas_too_large only once the job is reached, after earlier files are written. (b) file_stem replaces reserved characters but checks neither the component length (NTFS: 255 UTF-16 units) nor Windows device names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9, before the first dot, any case). A long name fails export_write in mid-run. `NUL.png` or `CON.png` may open the device instead of a file. On versions that map these names to devices, the bytes are discarded or printed, and the receipt lists a file that does not exist.
findings.scenario: (a) Two artboards: 'a' 64 by 64 first, then 'b' 12000 by 12000, both with [{format: PNG, constraint: WIDTH 16}]. a.png is written, then b refuses canvas_too_large. (b) A layer named 'nul' with [{format: PNG}].
findings.fix: In the plan, for a raster setting, also refuse export_too_large when u64(w)*u64(h) > MAX_VIEW_PIXELS. Refuse a new code export_name_invalid when the file name is over 255 UTF-16 units or its stem, case-folded and trimmed before the first '.', is a reserved device name. Add both to the hostile test, whose 'nothing written' assert already covers it.

findings.severity: low: a lost write with overwrite, and an accepted record that can never export
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/export_set.rs:439 (names keyed by file.to_lowercase()), :490 (write_atomic when overwrite); crates/hsk-studio-folio/src/export_settings.rs:331 (check_node_settings keys on the exact suffix)
findings.what: (a) The in-run collision check folds case with Rust's full to_lowercase. NTFS compares through its simple-uppercase table, so some names are one file on NTFS but two keys here: σ and ς both map to Σ, and 'aΣ.png' lowercases to 'aς.png' while 'aσ.png' stays as it is. With overwrite true, the second write_atomic replaces the first file and the receipt lists both. (b) Authoring (STU-IO-117 'refused at authoring time') compares suffixes case-sensitively. One node with [{PNG, suffix '@2x'}, {PNG, suffix '@2X'}] is accepted and stored, and every export.run of that node then refuses export_name_collision.
findings.scenario: (a) Layers named 'aσ' and 'aς', both PNG, export.run with overwrite true into an empty folder: two receipts, one file. (b) export.set_settings with the two suffixes above succeeds, then export.run refuses for good.
findings.fix: (a) In overwrite mode, use write_new for every path that did not exist at plan time (keep that set from the symlink_metadata probe). Then any fold mismatch refuses destination_exists instead of replacing a file. (b) In check_node_settings, key on (suffix.to_lowercase(), extension) or a per-char simple uppercase, so the authoring rule and the run rule agree.
